main_text.p: nem soluerit, Legatioque Abarorum ad Romanos, & quæcunque Ardagastus à Romanorum copiis passus fit. Porrò etiam quæ propè Tatimerum facta, fortitudoque Romanorum ducis Alexandri, & internecio Sclauorum quos adorti erant Romani. de natis monstris in vrbe regia, altero quadrupede, altero bicipite. quomodo Priscus remotus fit à bello Europæo, deque Theodoro Legato misso ad Chaganum à Prisco, eiusque prudentia & dexteritate.

SEPTIMVS liber memorat de perturbatione ordinis in exercitu Romano, fortitudinemque Romanorum contra Sclauos, siue vt antiquitus vocabantur, Getas: ac ea, quæ in ignobili quadam Thraciæ vrbe Petro eiusque subditis acciderunt. & quomodo Piragastus Sclauorum militum tribunus interemptus, Romanique in aquæ quæ illos fe-quuta est penuria fortiter se gesserint. & quomodo cum Petrus à Sclauis oppugnaretur, Priscus iterum fit factus Imperator exercitus. mortem Ioannis Ieiunatoris Constantinopolitani; deque acceptis à Mauricio pecuniis, eidemque data accepti Syngrapha. quaque pius princeps reuerentia, & verè Imperatoria erga mortuum vsus fit, deque pannosis aliquot per archiepiscopum eiusdem viri inuentis vestimentis. De Mauris collectis contra Carthaginem ciuitatem, & quomodo Gennadij virtute bellum fit extinctum. deq; Cometa qui per multos dies apparuit. de ciuili bello inter Turcas. & narratione instituta, de republica imperioq; Turca-

page.notes: Small-caps or enlarged initial letters ("S" of SEPTIMVS) are read as normal first letters. Line "Romaniquein aquæ quæillos fequuta" appears spaced irregularly in the scan; read as "Romanique in aquæ quæ illos fe-quuta". "pannosij" read as printed; the word may be "pannosis" with a worn letter, marked here as printed. "veltimentis" printed with a long s that looks like l; transcribed as "vestimentis". The right edge carries cropped fragments from the adjacent page, not transcribed.
